item.description: SiliconGym replaces ad hoc, single-task EDA feedback loops with a cross-task RL environment built on versioned workspaces, budgeted execution, and acceptance-gated scoring, with streaming dispatch overlapping tool checks and generation. Adoption costs substantial infrastructure: access to open-source or commercial EDA backends (commercial licenses are expensive), stateful workspace management, and parallel rollout orchestration beyond a single 24 GB GPU's typical use. It can fail if open-source-trained rewards do not transfer, since paired netlist evaluation shows open-source PPA gains do not always survive commercial synthesis, making the learned policy unreliable on the production toolchain. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: GRODE-RTL: Source-Mapped Dependency Views for LLM-Based RTL Repair
item.description: GRODE-RTL replaces flat source-level context (or full synthesized-graph exposure) given to a tool-using LLM agent for RTL repair with a compact, hop-partitioned dependency view built from the single-clock-stage fan-in cone of a suspect register, mapped back to editable source lines. Its costs are an EDA synthesis and netlist-to-source mapping pipeline, additional preprocessing latency per repair attempt, and the engineering complexity of maintaining that tooling, while the LLM itself remains an off-the-shelf API model. It can fail when the suspect register or anchor is misidentified, when faults span multiple clock stages beyond the extracted cone, and its evidence base is narrow: 30 faults and three specific models, so gains may not transfer to other designs, tools, or models. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: CompAct-Bench: A Benchmark for Working-Context Compaction in Long-Horizon Agent Tasks
item.description: CompAct-Bench evaluates LLM-based working-context compaction as a replacement for unbounded history accumulation in long-horizon agents, using controlled retention ratios across BrowseComp, SWE-bench, and an internal CompanyBench. Adopting compaction costs quality rather than infrastructure: even frontier models degrade downstream task accuracy under aggressive compression, and the iterative ratio-adjustment evaluation itself requires extra inference passes. After adoption, failures arise from distorted task state—unresolved issues rendered as conclusions and forgotten established results—causing incorrect decisions and redundant execution rather than mere information loss. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: STARK: Moving towards Personalized Agents That Truly Learn and Remember
item.description: STARK replaces flat episodic memory stores and retrieval-time episodic traversal with a dual-graph memory: an episodic graph of temporally, causally, and semantically linked events, plus an insight graph of LLM-extracted behavioral signals connected by the events that support them, with event-as-edge relational embeddings enabling cross-user transfer for cold-start users. It costs an LLM call per interaction for insight extraction and scoring, ongoing graph construction and maintenance, an embedding projection for transfer, and added system complexity relative to standard RAG-over-logs memory. It can fail through noisy or incorrect insight extraction that compounds as events accumulate, through embedding- or LLM-judge-based evaluation gains not transferring to the reader's domain, and through privacy or correctness risks when cross-user transfer infers insights for users with little data. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: VR-SparseQuant: Accurate FP4 Quantization with 2:4 Sparsity on Vera Rubin
item.description: VR-SparseQuant replaces dense W4A4 activation quantization with 2:4 structured-sparse FP4 execution on Vera Rubin hardware, using overlapping sparse streams to refine high-error activations while keeping native FP4 throughput. It costs a one-time offline scale-ratio calibration plus custom shared-weight GEMM kernels that only exist for unreleased VRFP4 hardware; the accuracy recovery relative to dense RTN W4A4 is demonstrated on a single model. It can fail on models whose activation error distributions do not align with the 2:4 sparsity pattern, and the perplexity gain does not guarantee downstream task quality. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Characterizing and Detecting Unfaithful Work Reports by Coding Agents
item.description: FaithDetector replaces manual review or blind acceptance of coding agents' work reports with an automated classifier that flags unfaithful claims (misreported observations, misattributed evidence, overstated success, faulty explanations). It costs an additional verification pass per report, adding latency and compute or API calls on top of the agent run, plus integration effort into the existing workflow. It can fail through false positives that erode developer trust and through false negatives that let overstated success claims pass, and its reported macro-F1 may not transfer to agents or domains outside the SWE-chat sample. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: When Safety Rationales Hallucinate: Diagnosing and Grounding Multimodal Safety Guards
item.description: TCG-RL replaces outcome-only supervised or preference training of rationale-generating safety guards with a contrastive RL objective that rewards tool use only when it improves grounding over a tool-free reference. It costs an RL training pipeline (reward computation against a tool-free baseline, tool-execution environment) rather than simple fine-tuning, increasing training complexity and compute beyond what one 24 GB GPU comfortably supports. It can fail if the tool-free reference is a weak comparator, if tool coverage does not match the fine-grained attributes and relations where hallucination concentrates, or if grounding rewards degrade classification calibration. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Efficient and Robust Drafting with Multi-Token Prediction
item.description: The method replaces a standalone small autoregressive draft model (or single-token Medusa-style heads) in speculative decoding with a single shared multi-token drafting head that reuses the target model's KV cache via zero-copy cross-attention, target activation injection, and clustered vocabulary projection. The cost is additional draft-head parameters and a parameter-efficient fine-tuning step to keep the drafter aligned with the target model, plus implementation complexity in KV-cache sharing and verification logic. It can fail when the drafter drifts out of alignment under domain shift or on unusual inputs, since acceptance rates collapse and speculative decoding then adds verification overhead without delivering speedup; results are also demonstrated only on Gemma 4, so transfer to other backbones is unverified. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: A Sparse Low-Rank Biclique Decomposition for Graphs
item.description: Signed biclique decomposition replaces dense low-rank-plus-sparse approximations (e.g., robust PCA) of graph adjacency matrices with a sum of sparse signed binary rank-one factors plus a sparse residual, and can substitute cuSPARSE SpMM with factorized multiplication. The cost is a greedy decomposition pass whose quality depends on the gain-based heuristic, and the factored form adds implementation complexity relative to calling a standard sparse library. It can fail on graphs lacking strong shared-neighborhood structure, where few bicliques are found, compression collapses, and the factorized SpMM may be slower than cuSPARSE. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Rank2Replace: VLM-Ranked Slot Replacement for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
item.description: Rank2Replace replaces standard training on raw images (or generic augmentation) with VLM-ranked, rank-preserving replacement of object-centric slots across images, so the small predictor learns to rely on task-relevant evidence rather than spurious cues. It costs a training-time pipeline dependency on pretrained VLMs and a frozen slot extractor, plus extra preprocessing and augmentation complexity, while inference remains unchanged and VLM-free. It can fail if the VLM misranks slot relevance, if slot extraction is poor on the target domain, or if the deployment shift differs from the benchmarked OOD splits, since gains are measured on only four datasets. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Harnessing Medical Visual-Language Models with Agentic Evidence Management
item.description: TUNE replaces the default agent pattern of passing raw segmentation masks directly to the model by explicitly managing which evidence to acquire, how to render it, and whether to accept the induced answer change. Its cost is added orchestration complexity and extra inference passes for presentation selection and update verification, rather than additional memory or training. It can fail when the harness accepts a mask-induced answer change that corrupts an initially correct prediction, and its gains may not transfer outside medical VQA domains with ground-truth masks. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Interpretable Prototype-Conditioned Adaptation for Weather Forecasting
item.description: ProtoCast replaces a monolithic neural weather forecaster with group-specific prototype banks, sparse mixtures of prototype-specific low-rank correction operators, and gated cross-group attention, jointly trained from scratch with prototypes refit each epoch. The cost is substantial: from-scratch training on weather datasets, per-epoch prototype refitting, and added architectural complexity that exceeds a single 24 GB GPU budget for global-scale data and offers no benefit outside weather forecasting. Failure modes include unstable prototype-operator associations during training, prototype banks that fail to capture rare regimes (as implied by the need for deletion analysis), and corrections that may not transfer across regions or variables. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: HabitusMem: Belief Memory over Evolving User Preferences for LLM Agents
item.description: It replaces retrieval of raw interaction-history snippets with a trained writer that maintains belief records about the user, each carrying evidence, scope, and current-versus-outdated status, for a frozen agent. The cost is training and maintaining the writer model plus extra inference and record-management complexity at write time, since the target agent itself stays frozen. It can fail if the belief writer misjudges preference scope or staleness, if training tasks do not transfer to the deployed domain, or if the user base is too small or static to justify a trained component over simple history retrieval. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: One Schedule Does Not Fit All: Adaptive Inference Schedules for Diffusion Language Models
item.description: TCDA replaces the fixed denoising schedule of a diffusion language model with a task-calibrated schedule selected via simultaneous one-sided bootstrap bounds that certify utility and degeneration guardrails, deploying the cheapest certified candidate. It costs a calibration stage with paired data, candidate samplers, and bootstrap computation, plus a fallback to the full schedule when no candidate certifies; runtime overhead itself is minimal. It can fail if calibration data is unrepresentative of production traffic, if the utility tolerance or guardrails are mis-set (with false certification up to the nominal alpha, observed below 2%), or if unconditional generation comparisons are confounded by the ELF sampler's randomized time grid. 1 independent implementation, 159 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Kameleo: In-Situ Activation-Precision Selection for Bit-Serial LLM Accelerators
item.description: Kameleo replaces offline perplexity-driven calibration of per-layer activation precision with runtime in-situ selection on a bit-serial accelerator, using a local proxy that compares each GEMM's reduced- and full-precision outputs. The cost is confined to custom hardware: a two-pass precision-setting phase over the first tokens plus 3.7% accelerator area, with MXU prefill cycles reduced 2.11-2.34x at a 1% perplexity budget. It can fail where the local proxy diverges from global perplexity on out-of-distribution workloads, and its gains are inaccessible on commodity GPUs without the underlying bit-serial datapath. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.
